The minimum daily intake for VitaminA(ug) is reduced by 20%.
A camp is removed from the network, eliminating its beneficiary population and associated ration and flow decisions.
The number of beneficiaries in a camp affects the total ration demand, which in turn impacts procurement and transport costs due to changes in total food requirements.
The plan changes due to the introduction of a purchase limit on food bought per supplier per day.
A floor on the total ration per person in Hassakeh camp is introduced, requiring the sum of rations across all foods to be at least 6.1 units per person per day.
Transport cost increases by 25% across all road links, affecting the total shipping cost in the supply chain.
